subject: 20261130-caching-pricing-hit-rate-final-qualification
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.example>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia@fintechco.com>, Daniel Cho <daniel@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.example>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.example>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 16:10:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call recap & pricing next steps — caching assumptions and target $/1M tokens

Hi Sofia / Daniel —

Great to meet today. Quick recap of what we covered and the proposals from Redwood so we can align on next steps: 

Summary of ask
- FinTech Co is evaluating Redwood for document-centric chat and transaction summarization. Primary goal: keep latency <= 250ms and control monthly spend while serving ~200M tokens/month initially with growth to ~1B tokens over 6–9 months.

High-level pricing targets discussed
- Target effective unit target: ~ $850 / 1M tokens (post-caching) as a goal for the initial contract.
- Budget range indicated on the call: $10k–$25k/month to start (scales with usage).

Caching assumptions we propose for pricing
- Prefix + session cache strategy: we expect a large fraction of tokens to be cacheable (system prompts, repeated prefixes, template responses).
- We used an initial conservative hit-rate band of 35%–55% for pricing scenarios. For your workload (highly repetitive templates), our estimate centers at ~50% prefix/session hit rate.
- Effective price example: list price at $1,700 / 1M tokens (uncached). With 50% hit rate, effective cost ≈ $850 / 1M tokens.
- If hit rate ends up lower (35%), effective ≈ $1,105 / 1M tokens; if higher (60%), effective ≈ $680 / 1M tokens.

Assumptions we used in the attached model (cache-hit-rate-model.xlsx)
- Token distribution: 60% response tokens, 40% prompt tokens; 30–40% of prompt tokens are steady prefixes; session lengths averaging 8 turns; recurring user templates.
- Cache TTL: 24 hours for session-level cache by default; ability to pin prefixes for longer if desired (impacts invalidation risk).
- De-duplication: prefix normalization applied to remove per-user ids before caching.

Next steps (agreed on call)
1) Redwood to share the detailed pricing sheet + cache model (attached). ACTION: Marissa — attached.
2) FinTech to share 3 representative prompt+response samples and an anonymized token histogram so we can run a tailored hit-rate simulation. ACTION: Sofia/Daniel.
3) Technical deep-dive on caching/TTL and integration patterns (Marcus to lead). Proposed dates: Nov 30–Dec 2. ACTION: Marcus — propose slots.
4) Procurement: we can draft an initial 3-month commitment with a mid-term review to re-benchmark effective $/1M once real traffic is available.

Please let me know if I missed anything. If the numbers above align, I’ll lock in tentative slots for the technical deep-dive and send an updated pricing sheet with line-by-line assumptions.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.example | (555) 555-0112

Attachments: RDW-pricing-sheet-Nov2026.pdf, cache-hit-rate-model.xlsx

- The 200M tokens/month initial is representative of the pilot — we expect concentrated bursts during statement runs.
- The 50% hit-rate assumption is optimistic but plausible given our heavy use of templates. We will share the sample prompts and a token histogram by EOD Monday.
- Procurement prefers a clear example of the effective monthly spend at 35%, 50%, and 60% hit rates (line items for uncached tokens, cached token hit credits, and any marginal costs).

Would you be able to surface a simple table in the pricing PDF that shows the three hit-rate scenarios and the resulting effective $/1M tokens and a sample monthly cost for 200M tokens? That will help our CFO.

Hi Sofia / Daniel —

Thanks for the confirmation and for sharing the prompt samples. Quick update on next steps and a small table inline so your CFO has what they asked for: 

Pricing scenarios (list price = $1,700 / 1M tokens)
- 35% hit rate -> effective price ≈ $1,105 / 1M tokens -> monthly for 200M tokens ≈ $221,000
- 50% hit rate -> effective price ≈ $850 / 1M tokens -> monthly for 200M tokens ≈ $170,000
- 60% hit rate -> effective price ≈ $680 / 1M tokens -> monthly for 200M tokens ≈ $136,000

Notes: the effective price is computed with a simple model where cached hits are billed at $0 (we apply caching credits), and uncached tokens billed at list price. We provide additional levers (bundled reserved capacity or committed usage tiers) that can further reduce the uncached list price if FinTech signs a reserved capacity commitment.

Next items: 
- Marcus will run the detailed simulation once we get your histogram and upload the populated spreadsheet to the HubSpot deal (RDW-2026-0456).
- Technical deep-dive proposed slots: Tue Nov 30 16:00–17:00 PST or Wed Dec 1 09:00–10:00 PST. Marcus — can you confirm availability?
- Once we have a quantified hit-rate from your samples we’ll produce a 3-month pilot quote and a recommended reserved capacity sizing to meet your latency and budget targets.

If that looks good I’ll book the slot and loop in our procurement lead to draft an initial term sheet.

Best,
Marissa Cole
